# Seizing the Decade

September 13, 2022

### The International Decade of Indigenous Languages amplifies SIL’s mission to support language communities.

The start to the International Decade of Indigenous Languages (IDIL) represents an exciting opportunity for SIL to continue the work we have been committed to for more than 85 years. Declared by the United Nations General Assembly in 2019, [IDIL](https://en.unesco.org/idil2022-2032) “aims at ensuring indigenous peoples’ right to preserve, revitalize and promote their languages, and mainstreaming linguistic diversity and multilingualism aspects into the sustainable development efforts.”

Although SIL does not exclusively work with indigenous languages* as they are traditionally defined, SIL is committed to working alongside all marginalized language communities as they pursue their language-related goals. With research showing that nearly 40% of the world’s language communities lack meaningful access to important resources in their own languages, this represents an exciting time for communities around the world to build more opportunities to use the languages they value most in accomplishing the things important to them.

IDIL gives us a dedicated opportunity to raise awareness of the challenges language communities face and the many benefits local languages contribute to multiple spheres of society. This includes education, healthcare, ecological management and spiritual development, each of which constitutes an area where SIL is involved in work alongside communities to develop language-related solutions. Supporting under-resourced languages digitally by developing digital tools to facilitate the production and availability of local language resources online is another important SIL activity.

Marginalized communities of all kinds often represent the most vulnerable populations, facing unique challenges and risks. Language is a powerful tool to both amplify their voices as they pursue their goals and mitigate the challenges they face. Additionally, utilizing the languages that mean the most to them in everyday life maximizes the efficacy of environmental and social healing programs, like trauma healing workshops and the [Faith and Farming](https://www.sil.org/blog/dignity-dirt) initiative recently introduced in Africa.

Celebrating the world’s indigenous languages provides us with a crucial opportunity to work towards their preservation as well. According to a recent [State of the Environment](https://soe.dcceew.gov.au/climate/management/national-and-international-frameworks#-cli-21-figure-21-indigenous-peoples-and-the-environment) report released by the Australian government, indigenous peoples protect 80% of the world’s biodiversity. As such, these communities and their languages serve as irreplaceable records of information on the natural environment, medicine and human history. As they diminish, so do the potential benefits to all mankind.

Partnership—with communities, governments and other development agencies—is a key strategy for maximizing impact and results as we work together to better contribute to the outputs of IDIL. As the momentum gathered around IDIL contributes to a more conducive environment for partnership and more extensive opportunities to support these communities and their languages, SIL is ready and eager to participate.

[![Image 7: IDIL Logo](https://www.silglobal.site/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/decade_of_indigenous_languages_logo_en_mesa_de_trabajo_1-scaled.png)](https://www.sil.org/idil)  
(Click here to learn more about SIL’s involvement in IDIL)

* * *

*The term “indigenous” is interpreted differently among individual nations and relevant stakeholders. UNESCO’s Global Action plan for IDIL adopts a broader definition that supports “principles of non-discrimination, the right to development and inclusion, and an equal and fair chance to access opportunities” for speakers and signers of lesser-used languages. SIL’s continuing commitment to supporting a wide range of linguistically marginalized communities—including indigenous populations—gives us particular opportunities to contribute towards the efforts of IDIL. # About Us

![Image 7](https://www.silglobal.site/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/481819738_1028106992678530_3781395677498780286_n-e1755637541957.jpg)

##### Serving the world’s language communities since 1934.

#### SIL Global is a community of local organizations that partner with minority language communities to help them use their languages to know God, learn freely, and live with dignity.

Many people around the world face hardship and discrimination because of the languages they speak or sign. We walk alongside 1,572 language communities in 119 countries to help turn those barriers of exclusion into bridges for flourishing.

## Our Vision & Mission

#### **A century-long calling, still alive today.**

###### VISION

We long to see people flourishing in community using the languages they value most.

###### MISSION

Inspired by God’s love, we advocate, build capacity, and work with local communities to apply language expertise that advances meaningful development, education, and engagement with Scripture.

## Our Why

Our faith inspires and informs our commitment to expand possibilities for people to thrive. We believe all people are created by God and given language as a means for flourishing. Through language, we understand who we are, experience relationships and explore life’s most important questions.

As followers of Jesus, we believe:

*   All people are important.That’s why we care about all languages.

# About Us

![Image 7](https://www.silglobal.site/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/481819738_1028106992678530_3781395677498780286_n-e1755637541957.jpg)

##### Serving the world’s language communities since 1934.

#### SIL Global is a community of local organizations that partner with minority language communities to help them use their languages to know God, learn freely, and live with dignity.

Many people around the world face hardship and discrimination because of the languages they speak or sign. We walk alongside 1,572 language communities in 119 countries to help turn those barriers of exclusion into bridges for flourishing.

## Our Vision & Mission

#### **A century-long calling, still alive today.**

###### VISION

We long to see people flourishing in community using the languages they value most.

###### MISSION

Inspired by God’s love, we advocate, build capacity, and work with local communities to apply language expertise that advances meaningful development, education, and engagement with Scripture.

## Our Why

Our faith inspires and informs our commitment to expand possibilities for people to thrive. We believe all people are created by God and given language as a means for flourishing. Through language, we understand who we are, experience relationships and explore life’s most important questions.

As followers of Jesus, we believe:

*   All people are important.That’s why we care about all languages.
*   Relationship with God is precious.That’s why we pray, love the Bible and support its translation so others can have the same opportunities to know God better.
*   All aspects of a person’s life matter.That’s why we work toward language solutions that advance learning, health, justice, reconciliation and spiritual growth.
